findings.fix: Pass the profile as one token: `-presentation-profile=$PresentationProfile` (the spec's `-presentation-profile=` form), so an empty value stays a valid flag on Windows PowerShell 5.1.
findings.claim: install.ps1 forwards the profile as two argv words (`-presentation-profile $PresentationProfile`) instead of the spec's `-presentation-profile=<id>` form; with the default empty $PresentationProfile, Windows PowerShell 5.1 (what install.bat launches via `powershell`) drops the empty-string argument to the native exe, so configserver.exe receives a trailing `-presentation-profile` with no value, Go's flag.Parse exits 2 ('flag needs an argument'), and install.ps1 throws 'configserver -install failed (exit 2)' — every default from-source Windows install fails.
findings.evidence: Re-read install.ps1 L3-9 (param PresentationProfile defaults to "") and L64 (`& bin\configserver.exe -install ... -peek-control-port $PeekControlPort -presentation-profile $PresentationProfile 2>&1`), L66 (non-zero exit throws). install.bat L4 runs `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1` = Windows PowerShell 5.1, which omits empty-string arguments to native commands (fixed only by PS 7.3's PSNativeCommandArgumentPassing). cmd/configserver/main.go L59 declares `-presentation-profile` as flag.String and L67 calls flag.Parse() before the L116 install branch, so a value-less final `-presentation-profile` aborts with exit 2. correctness-34 requires forwarding as `-presentation-profile=` (single token), which would survive an empty value; the .iss path (ProfileArg ` -presentation-profile=de`) uses that form and is unaffected. Note: the line predates the review base (introduced in e258ac1, an ancestor of b4981b8); it is reported because the walk item fails at the head and install.ps1 is a changed file in this chunk.
